name: Beef lasagne
summary: Layers of dry lasagne sheets, beef bolognese sauce and white sauce, baked under mozzarella and Parmesan.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Have the bolognese sauce and white sauce warm or at room temperature.

Spread a thin layer of bolognese sauce over the base of the baking dish. Cover with a layer of dry lasagne sheets (250 g in all), then bolognese, then a thin layer of white sauce. Repeat to make 3 or 4 layers, finishing with sheets covered by the rest of the white sauce.

Scatter over the grated mozzarella and Parmesan. Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 20 to 25 minutes more until golden and the sheets are tender when pierced with a knife.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into 6. Leftover portions keep 3 days in the fridge or can be frozen.
notes: Uses a full batch each of bolognese sauce and white sauce. Dry no-precook sheets soften in the sauce, so the dry pasta record is used. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Vegetable lasagne
summary: Lasagne layered with roasted courgette, aubergine and pepper in tomato sauce, spinach and white sauce.
method: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Cut the courgette, aubergine, red pepper and onion into 2 cm chunks, toss with the olive oil, salt and black pepper on 2 roasting trays and roast for 25 to 30 minutes until tender. Lower the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Stir the roasted vegetables and the spinach into the warm tomato sauce; the spinach will wilt in the heat.

Spread a little of the vegetable sauce over the base of the baking dish. Layer with dry lasagne sheets (250 g in all), more vegetable sauce and a thin layer of white sauce; repeat to make 3 or 4 layers, finishing with sheets covered by the rest of the white sauce.

Scatter with the grated mozzarella and Parmesan, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and the sheets are tender. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
notes: A variant of beef lasagne: roasted vegetables in tomato sauce replace the bolognese sauce. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Spinach and ricotta cannelloni
summary: Cannelloni tubes filled with spinach, ricotta and Parmesan, baked on tomato sauce under white sauce.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Wilt the spinach in a large pan with a splash of water, cool, then squeeze it dry and chop.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, egg, half the grated Parmesan, the nutmeg, salt and black pepper. Spoon or pipe into the 180 g dry cannelloni tubes (about 16).
Spread the tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish and lay the filled tubes on top in one layer. Pour over the white sauce to cover them completely and scatter with the rest of the Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden and bubbling and the pasta is tender.
notes: Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Macaroni cheese
summary: Macaroni in Cheddar cheese sauce, baked under a crisp Cheddar and breadcrumb crust.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the 250 g dry macaroni in a large pan of boiling water for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Stir the macaroni into the warm cheese sauce and tip into the baking dish.
Mix the grated Cheddar with the breadcrumbs and scatter over the top. Lay over slices of tomato if you like.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Uses a full batch of cheese sauce. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Tuna pasta bake
summary: Penne, tinned tuna, sweetcorn and spring onions in cheese sauce, baked under Cheddar.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the 300 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Mix the penne with the cheese sauce, the drained tuna (two tins) in flakes, the drained sweetcorn and the sliced spring onions, and tip into the baking dish.
Scatter with the grated Cheddar and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: Uses tuna in water, drained. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Chicken pasta bake
summary: Penne with pan-fried chicken and broccoli in cheese sauce, baked under Cheddar.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the 250 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 2 minutes less than the pack says, adding the broccoli florets for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Meanwhile cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces, season with the salt and black pepper and fry in the olive oil for 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through.
Mix the penne, broccoli and chicken with the cheese sauce, tip into the baking dish and scatter with the grated Cheddar.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: A variant of tuna pasta bake: chicken and broccoli replace the tuna, sweetcorn and spring onions. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Vegetable pasta bake
summary: Fusilli with pan-fried courgette, pepper and red onion in tomato sauce, baked under mozzarella.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the chopped courgette, red pepper and red onion over a medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until softened and lightly coloured. Season with the oregano, salt and black pepper.
Meanwhile cook the 300 g dry fusilli in a large pan of boiling water for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Mix the fusilli, vegetables and tomato sauce in the baking dish. Top with the torn mozzarella and grated Parmesan.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is golden.
notes: Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Aubergine pasta bake
summary: Penne with roasted aubergines, tomato sauce and basil, dotted with ricotta and baked under mozzarella.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the aubergines into 2 cm cubes, toss with the olive oil and salt and roast on a tray for 25 minutes until golden and soft.
Meanwhile cook the 300 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
Mix the penne, aubergines, tomato sauce and torn basil in the baking dish. Dot with spoonfuls of ricotta and top with the torn mozzarella and grated Parmesan.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden.
notes: A variant of vegetable pasta bake: roasted aubergine and ricotta replace the mixed pan-fried vegetables. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Baked gnocchi
summary: Potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with basil under melting mozzarella and Parmesan.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cook the gnocchi in a large pan of boiling water just until they float, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Mix the gnocchi with the tomato sauce and torn basil in the baking dish, and top with the torn mozzarella and grated Parmesan.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is golden in spots.
notes: Uses a full batch each of potato gnocchi and tomato pasta sauce. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Stuffed pasta shells
summary: Large pasta shells filled with ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan and parsley, baked in tomato sauce.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the 250 g dry pasta shells (about 26 conchiglioni) in a large pan of boiling water for 3 minutes less than the pack says so they stay firm. Drain, rinse under cold water and lay out on a tray.
Mix the ricotta with half the grated mozzarella, half the grated Parmesan, the egg, the chopped parsley, the grated garlic, salt and black pepper.
Spread the tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish. Fill each shell with a spoonful of the ricotta mixture and sit them in the sauce, filling side up.
Scatter with the rest of the mozzarella and Parmesan, cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 to 15 minutes until golden.
notes: Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Baked rice with mince
summary: Rice baked in the oven with beef bolognese sauce, tomatoes and stock under a Parmesan crust.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Dissolve the stock cube in 600 ml boiling water.
In the deep baking dish, mix the 400 g dry rice (rinsed) with the bolognese sauce, the chopped tomatoes and the hot stock.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Stir gently, check the rice and add a splash of boiling water if it looks dry.
Scatter with the grated Parmesan and bake uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the top is golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: A plain everyday version; the Maltese ross il-forn is its own recipe. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Chicken and rice casserole
summary: Paprika chicken thighs baked with rice, pepper, tomatoes and stock in one pot, finished with peas.
equipment: large flameproof casserole with a lid
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Cut the boneless chicken thighs in half and season with the paprika, salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in the casserole and brown the chicken for 5 minutes, then lift out.
Add the sliced onion and red pepper and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Stir in the 250 g dry rice, the chopped tomatoes and the stock cube dissolved in 500 ml boiling water. Return the chicken, bring to a simmer, cover and bake for 30 minutes.
Stir in the frozen peas, cover and bake for 10 minutes more until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed. Scatter with the chopped parsley.

name: Stuffed peppers
summary: Pepper halves filled with rice and beef bolognese sauce, baked under mozzarella.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the 120 g dry rice in boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Halve the peppers (4 large) lengthways through the stalk and remove the seeds. Brush with the olive oil, sit cut side up in the baking dish and bake for 10 minutes to soften.
Mix the rice with the warm bolognese sauce and the chopped parsley and pile into the pepper halves.
Top with the grated mozzarella, add a splash of water to the dish, cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 minutes until golden.
notes: Pepper weight is trimmed and deseeded. Two halves per serving. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Cottage pie
summary: Beef mince and vegetables in a rich gravy, baked under buttery mash and Cheddar.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Add the beef mince, turn up the heat and brown, breaking it up.

Stir in the plain flour and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme and the stock cube dissolved in 400 ml boiling water. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until thick, stir in the frozen peas and season with half the salt and the black pepper. Tip into the baking dish.
Meanwhile boil the peeled, chunked potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and the rest of the salt until smooth.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spread the mash over the mince, rough up the top with a fork and scatter with the grated Cheddar. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes.

name: Shepherd's pie
summary: Lamb mince and vegetables in gravy, baked under buttery mash and Cheddar.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Add the lamb mince, turn up the heat and brown, breaking it up; spoon off any excess fat if you like.

Stir in the plain flour and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme and the stock cube dissolved in 400 ml boiling water. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until thick, stir in the frozen peas and season with half the salt and the black pepper. Tip into the baking dish.
Meanwhile boil the peeled, chunked potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and the rest of the salt until smooth.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spread the mash over the lamb, rough up the top with a fork and scatter with the grated Cheddar. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden. Rest for 5 minutes.
notes: A variant of cottage pie with lamb mince instead of beef. Fat spooned off is not subtracted from the totals.

name: Moussaka
summary: Roasted aubergine and potato layered with cinnamon-spiced lamb and tomato, topped with an egg-enriched white sauce.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Slice the aubergines 1 cm thick and the peeled potatoes 5 mm thick. Brush with most of the olive oil, sprinkle with a little of the salt and roast on 2 trays for 20 to 25 minutes until soft and golden.

Meanwhile heat the rest of the olive oil in a large pan and soften the chopped onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, then the lamb mince and brown it. Add the cinnamon, oregano, tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, the red wine if using, the rest of the salt and the black pepper, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until thick.
Beat the egg and half the grated Parmesan into the white sauce.

Lower the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Layer the potatoes over the base of the baking dish, then half the aubergines, all the lamb sauce and the rest of the aubergines. Pour over the white sauce and scatter with the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.
notes: Parmesan stands in for a Greek hard cheese. The wine is optional and left out of the totals unless chosen. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Aubergine parmigiana-style bake
summary: Layers of roasted aubergine slices, tomato sauce, mozzarella, basil and Parmesan.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Slice the aubergines lengthways 1 cm thick, brush both sides with the olive oil, sprinkle with the salt and roast on 2 trays for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and golden.

Lower the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Spread a little tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish, then layer the aubergines with more tomato sauce, torn mozzarella, basil leaves and grated Parmesan. Repeat to make 3 layers, finishing with sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: The aubergines are roasted rather than fried, so less oil is used than in many versions. Times assume the component sauces are already made.

name: Chicken enchiladas
summary: Flour tortillas rolled around spiced chicken, pepper and black beans, baked in a tomato sauce under Cheddar.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Heat the sunflower oil in a large frying pan and cook the sliced onion and red pepper for 6 minutes. Add the diced chicken breast and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through.
Add the garlic, cumin, chilli powder and paprika for 1 minute, then stir in the drained black beans, half the salt and 4 tablespoons of the passata.

Season the rest of the passata with the rest of the salt and spread a third of it over the base of the baking dish. Divide the filling between the 8 small (20 cm) flour tortillas, roll them up and lay them seam side down in the dish.

Pour over the remaining passata and scatter with the grated Cheddar. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling. Scatter with coriander and serve with the salsa, and the guacamole and soured cream if you like.
notes: Two enchiladas per serving. Uses the tomato salsa component; the guacamole component is an optional extra.

name: Toad in the hole
summary: Pork sausages baked in a puffed Yorkshire pudding batter, served with gravy.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Whisk the plain flour and salt with the eggs, then gradually whisk in the milk to a smooth batter. Leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Put the sausages (8) and the sunflower oil in the roasting tin and roast for 15 minutes until browned.
Working quickly, pour the batter around the sausages in the hot fat and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until risen and deep golden; don't open the oven door for the first 20 minutes.
Serve straight away with the gravy, warmed.
notes: The catalogue sausage is a generic pork sausage record; check your sausages' label if they differ. Times assume the gravy is made while the batter bakes.

name: Baked feta pasta
summary: A block of feta roasted with cherry tomatoes, garlic and olive oil, then stirred into fusilli.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the cherry tomatoes in the baking dish with the olive oil, peeled garlic cloves, chilli flakes, oregano and black pepper and toss. Sit the block of feta in the middle and turn it to coat in the oil.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the tomatoes have burst and the feta is soft and golden at the edges.
Meanwhile cook the 300 g dry fusilli in a large pan of boiling water until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Squash the garlic and mash the feta and tomatoes together into a sauce, then stir in the fusilli with a splash of the cooking water and the torn basil.

name: Leeks and ham in cheese sauce
summary: Tender leeks wrapped in ham, baked in cheese sauce under a Cheddar and breadcrumb crust.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Trim the leeks and cut each in half to fit the dish. Simmer in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes until tender, then drain well and pat dry.
Wrap each piece of leek in a slice of ham and lay them side by side in the baking dish.
Pour over the warm cheese sauce and scatter with the grated Cheddar mixed with the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: Leek weight is trimmed weight (about 4 medium leeks). Good with crusty bread or boiled potatoes. Times assume the component sauces are already made.
